name: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids II)
summary_goal: Study how flames on PMMA solid fuel behave in microgravity under controlled flow, including how they respond when flow is reduced until extinction.

sources.locator: provisional description; locator to be verified

limitations: Provisional team-curated record; values are verified against the cited source only after review.
All numeric conditions (diameter, thickness, flow velocity, O2, pressure) are unknown in this corpus.
Exemplar tests are structural placeholders, not measurements.

text_chunks.text: BASS-II investigates how PMMA (acrylic) solid-fuel flames spread and extinguish in microgravity aboard the International Space Station, using cylindrical rod and flat sheet samples in a controlled flow.

Flow-reduction-to-extinction protocol: the sample is ignited, a flame is established and spreads, then the oxidizer flow is reduced until the flame extinguishes. The flow history, not only the starting flow, is part of the condition.
Relevant to spacecraft fire prevention: how low a ventilation flow must fall before a solid-fuel flame goes out in microgravity, for rod and sheet geometry.

Exemplar records cover comparison edge cases: same initial flow with different flow history, operator termination versus extinction, different thickness and substrate, ambient oxygen versus oxidizer stream, simulated versus actual microgravity.

text_chunks.text: Saffire-I ignited a large cotton-fiberglass fabric sample remotely in an uncrewed Cygnus vehicle after ISS departure to study flame spread over a large sample in microgravity.
Large-scale spread data address whether small-sample results transfer to spacecraft-scale fires: prevention and material selection.

text_chunks.text: FLEX burns isolated fuel droplets (for example n-heptane and methanol) in microgravity while varying the chamber atmosphere to study extinguishment, relevant to fire suppression agents.
Gas-phase extinguishment limits of spherical droplet flames inform suppression concepts; droplet geometry is not a solid-fuel geometry.

text_chunks.text: FLEX-2 studied droplet combustion and observed that after the visible hot flame went out, droplets could continue to burn as cool flames with no visible flame.
A flame that is visually extinguished may still be burning: hot extinction is not necessarily final extinction. Relevant to detection and suppression judgements.
